short: A heavy frigate of the United States Navy, noted for her durability in the War of 1812.
full:
Launched in 1797, the USS Constitution was one of the original six frigates authorised by the Naval Act of 1794. Built with a robust hull made of densely packed live oak, she was larger and more heavily armed than standard frigates of the era. She first saw action during the Quasi-War with France and the First Barbary War.

She achieved widespread fame during the War of 1812, defeating five British warships and capturing numerous merchant vessels. During a fierce battle with HMS Guerriere, British cannonballs were seen bouncing off her sturdy wooden sides, earning her the enduring nickname "Old Ironsides". She remains afloat as the world's oldest commissioned naval vessel still sailing.
